name: Erik Costa

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm a senior researcher from the Work Futures Panel, an independent group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What did your workday involve yesterday?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: A building supplier had two versions of the same delivery note, so I had to trace which one the warehouse actually used before I finished its tax return. I'm 43, an experienced mid-level accountant at Ledger House with a bachelor's degree and a professional accountancy qualification; I'm competent, not the firm's star. I like explaining a clean answer to the supplier, and I hate the afternoon when the phone rings again because one pallet was counted twice.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is life around work like, and do you use AI now?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Lila is an occupational therapist, and our children are eight and thirteen; we have a mortgage. Ledger House pays me well for this level, we have nine months of expenses saved, and there are plenty of accounting firms nearby. I use AI now and then for a draft only after someone else has tried the tool, then check every delivery note myself. I support worker representation and clear rules for client data, but I want evidence before any new system becomes a target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau — Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the team a quicker note search is useful if we can still show a supplier the original. I would ask whether the saved minutes go to proper checking or a higher target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our salaries and nine-month reserve keep the mortgage secure in this quiet picture. I'm still only average at this work, so I wouldn't ignore a change in reviews, but I don't expect my paid hours to fall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep preparing the supplier accounts and checking AI-assisted drafts against delivery notes. In the first year I'd add one hundred a month from pay to our reserve and bring the target question to the staff committee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about our income. I can raise a small concern without fearing next month's loan payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does the original note prove?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One version showed twelve pallets and the other showed eleven after a return. I followed the warehouse stamp before the tax figure went out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What will you ask the staff committee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Whether the firm will measure corrected errors as well as minutes saved. I would bring one delivery-note error to the staff committee, not a speech about machines.

say: I would ask for **corrected-error measures** beside time saved.
I would show the supplier the **original delivery note**.
think: Our **mortgage feels secure** with two wages and nine months saved.
I do not expect my **hours to fall** in a plateau.
do: Keep checking **delivery notes** behind supplier accounts and occasional AI drafts.
Save **one hundred monthly** from pay into our reserve.
Raise **review targets** at the staff committee.
feel: He feels **calm** about income while asking about targets.
S0.quote: I would bring one delivery-note error to the staff committee, not a speech about machines.
fieldNote: His strong reserve and high pay support a **calm baseline**, even with a mortgage and children.
He uses AI **occasionally after testing** and takes a concrete delivery-note error to the committee.

steps.text: Keep checking supplier delivery notes behind AI-assisted drafts
Add one hundred monthly from pay to household reserve
Raise review target question at staff committee with delivery-note example

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption — Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the partners to publish the error rate before moving more supplier returns to software. The staff committee should have a say if the review rota or trainee posts change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Checking, writing and answering supplier questions are most of my day, so I could lose paid hours even at a firm that keeps its clients. Nine months saved gives our family time, but it wouldn't make my high wage easy to replace.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd join the staff committee's request for a written hours plan and paid training, and test the approved tool on ten closed supplier files if the firm funds a supervised afternoon. In the first year of steady change, if my paid hours fall, I'd apply for posted accounts jobs at nearby firms only with a written salary and start date that cover our fixed bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own wage, though I can use the reserve to search. A smaller rota can reach an average accountant quickly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The senior reviewer who knows the supplier files should sign the error list. I would not put live client details into a trial simply to show I am keen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the funded afternoon is refused?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep my current returns and ask the committee to record the refusal. I could read the firm's free examples on my own time, but I would not pretend a request taught me the software.

say: I would demand **published error rates** before changing reviews.
I would ask the **staff committee** to review rota and trainee changes.
think: My **paid hours** could fall because desk work is exposed.
A new firm may not match my **high wage**.
do: Request a **written hours plan** through the staff committee.
Test **ten closed supplier files** on paid supervised time if approved.
Apply for **posted local accounts** work if paid hours fall.
feel: He feels **anxious** about a cut to his own high wage.
S1.quote: A smaller rota can reach an average accountant quickly.
fieldNote: He asks for **paid training** and error evidence before any rota decision.
The job search needs a **written wage** and posted role; a refusal leaves him on paid returns.

steps.text: Join staff committee request for written hours plan and paid training
Test ten closed supplier files during paid supervised session if approved
Apply for posted local accounting after hour cut; require written bill-covering salary and start date
Keep paid returns and free examples if training refused; ask committee to record refusal

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028 — Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the staff that full AGI in 2028 reaches our accounts desk before robots can do hands-on work around 2031. We should demand notice and a named reviewer for each machine-prepared return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect Ledger House to cut accounting posts when cheap AGI handles checks and tax letters; my average performance means I could be among them. Lila's hands-on therapy work may face robots later, so even nine months saved would not cover two long searches.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'd add two hundred to our monthly reserve deposit and ask the committee for a written notice period before cuts. In the first year after 2028, if my post ends, I'd apply for posted salaried supplier-finance jobs at local builders and keep any paid Ledger House reconciliation hours until a written wage and start date are agreed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, though the prospect is serious. I expect posts to go, but I have savings and nearby employers to try before we miss a mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept a much lower wage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after comparing the written offer with the mortgage, school costs and Lila's hours. I would not move the family on the strength of a vacancy notice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the committee ask for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At least a month's notice, paid placement help and a named person to answer tax disputes. I would go to the meeting and put those three requests in writing.

say: I would demand **one month’s notice** and a named reviewer.
I would ask for **paid placement help** before cuts.
think: My **average standing** could put me among post cuts in 2028.
Lila’s **therapy work** may face robots around 2031.
do: Add **two hundred monthly** to the family reserve now.
Join the **staff committee** request for notice and paid placement.
Seek **posted supplier-finance work** after 2028 job loss, keeping paid reconciliation hours until written wage/start are agreed.
feel: He feels **anxious** about possible job loss, with a usable reserve.
S2.quote: I would not move the family on the strength of a vacancy notice.
fieldNote: He sees **2028 desk risk** for himself and later hands-on robot exposure for Lila.
His nine-month reserve and local firms allow an **anxious search**, while the committee requests concrete notice and placement help.

steps.text: Add two hundred monthly to existing household reserve
Join staff committee request for month notice and paid placement
Apply for posted salaried supplier-finance if job ends; require written bill-covering wage and start
Keep paid Ledger House hours until written replacement wage and start date are agreed

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031 — Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years gives the committee time to bargain for a proper job path and gives clients time to see what they still need checked. I would not promise an accountant has a permanent edge over AGI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 48 in 2031 I'd still have children at school and a mortgage, and full AGI could do the supplier checking I sell. I might have a year of savings by then. A reserve is not a career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd set a twelve-month savings target by adding two hundred a month from pay and take a paid slot checking AI error logs if the firm assigns one. In the first year after 2031, if Ledger House cuts my paid hours, I'd apply for posted salaried procurement-accounting roles at supplier firms, keeping current hours until a written wage and start date are firm. The assigned paid slot would teach me how to audit the AI’s invoice matches.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, although five years gives us a chance to build cash and a work record. My children's school bills won't stop because the calendar was kinder.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would an error-log slot involve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd compare the machine's invoice match with a warehouse receipt and write down which rule failed. A manager would have to pay for the slot and review my first batch.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no slot is assigned?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep preparing the current supplier accounts and the savings transfer, and ask the committee for a staffing update. I wouldn't pay for private AI software just to look busy.

say: I would ask for a **paid error-log slot** with review.
I would press for a **staffing update** if no slot exists.
think: At **48 in 2031**, I still need a mortgage wage.
A larger **reserve** is no replacement for a career.
do: Save **two hundred monthly** toward twelve months of expenses.
Learn **AI error auditing** on assigned paid logs with manager review.
Seek **posted procurement-accounting work** after pay cuts, keeping current hours until written wage and start date are firm.
feel: He feels **anxious** despite five years to build cash and evidence.
S3.quote: A reserve is not a career.
fieldNote: The error-log duty needs **assigned paid hours** and manager review, so it is not speculative retraining.
He keeps **current accounts and savings** if no slot exists, then seeks only posted salaried work.

steps.text: Add two hundred monthly from pay until reserve covers twelve months
Learn AI error auditing on assigned paid logs with manager review if offered
Seek posted procurement-accounting after 2031 cut; keep current hours until written wage/start are firm
Keep paid supplier accounts and ask committee for staffing update if no error-log slot

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036 — Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say ten years is time to agree on fair notice and teach staff to question any automated tax figure. The partners should show the costs and fees each year, not wait until 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 in 2036 I would still need income, but a decade of high pay could reduce our mortgage and build more savings. AGI reaches my desk then; robots around 2039 could affect Lila's therapy work later, so two wages still matter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd pay an extra one hundred and fifty monthly against the mortgage while both wages hold and keep checking current supplier returns. In the first year after 2036, if the firm cuts my paid role, I'd apply for posted salaried procurement posts nearby and keep any funded Ledger House hours until a written wage and start date replace them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the long-term job, even with a better balance sheet. Ten years helps us reduce the loan, but I would still need a pay cheque at 53.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make you stop the extra loan payment?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If either of us lost paid hours, I'd hold that one hundred and fifty in cash for bills instead. Paying down debt is useful only while the kitchen is covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you retire early if the mortgage gets small?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, the children and our future bills still need wages. I would rather move to a paid procurement job than borrow from the reserve to stop working.

say: I would seek **fair notice** before any 2036 cuts to accounting staff or client review hours.
I would ask the partners for **yearly fee figures**.
think: At **53 in 2036**, I still need wage income.
Lila’s **2039 robot risk** could affect the other wage.
do: Pay **one hundred fifty** extra monthly off the mortgage while both wages hold.
Keep checking **supplier returns** against original delivery records.
Apply for **posted procurement roles** if my paid post is cut after 2036.
feel: He feels **uneasy** about long-term wages despite strong savings.
S4.quote: Ten years helps us reduce the loan, but I would still need a pay cheque at 53.
fieldNote: His decade plan uses high pay to **reduce mortgage debt**, stopping extra payments if either wage falls.
His 2036 fallback needs a **posted salaried role** and written terms while existing paid work continues.

steps.text: Pay one hundred fifty extra monthly off mortgage while both wages hold; stop if hours fall
Keep checking supplier returns against original delivery notes
Apply for posted procurement job after 2036 cut; require written wage/start and keep paid firm hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because ordinary reviews could disappear before the children finish school. A month's notice, paid placement help and a real salaried supplier role would help. Nine months of savings gives us breathing room; it doesn't tell us what the next job is.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who is paid to find a wrong tax figure after AI prepares the return. A client cannot appeal to a green tick on a screen.

headlineQuote: A client cannot appeal to a green tick on a screen.
portrait: Erik, **43**, is an average-skilled mid-level accountant at Ledger House with a bachelor’s degree and professional qualification.
His **high pay**, nine-month reserve and Lila’s therapy wage support two school-age children and a mortgage.
He uses AI **occasionally after colleagues** test it, with plenty of nearby accounting firms as possible alternatives.
He expects **2028 post cuts** and uses committee action, savings and posted roles rather than trusting a job title.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut his accounts role before the children finish school.
whatWouldHelp: **One month’s notice**, paid placement and a real salaried supplier role would help.
